cards.label: Bermondsey — James's unit
cards.text: You've carried {calcQty} time calc across London in a lunchbox. James weighs it on the scales before he says hello. Then he weighs it again.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "Correct." He counts £{calcPay} into an envelope and slides it across. "For the calc. We'll discuss the labour when there is some."
The Dial lies on a cloth beside the tin. The broken Movement is gone. Its seat has been cleaned until it shines, recently and with care.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "Recharge Movement, time-attuned. It can't hold much of a charge, but recharges quickly. When it works, that is."
"You look, you can touch, but be very, very careful. I'll tell you if you're about to do something stupid, and not before." He folds his arms and sits on the stool.
You work the calc the way you would a pearl, only slower. A spring takes shape under your fingers. You seat it in the Dial and give the collar a turn.

cards.label: It goes wrong
cards.text: Nothing. Then a dry crack. The spring loses its shape and the calc in it goes grey and dead, like cigarette ash. The Dial stays cold. That was {attemptCost} calc.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: He lifts the dead Movement out with tweezers and studies it. "Too fast at the end. You were thinking about the result." He sets it aside. "Try again."
The second allowance sits on the scales. If this one goes the same way, there is no third.

choices.label: Go slower
choices.result_text: You take the spring a turn at a time. James doesn't speak. Halfway through, you notice he has stopped tapping his foot.

choices.label: Ask what you did wrong
choices.result_text: "You finished it before it was finished." He taps the bench. "Again. Listen to it this time."

choices.label: Ask James to hold the Dial
choices.result_text: He picks it up without comment and holds it out in both hands. For possibly the first time ever, they aren't quite steady. You don't mention it.

cards.text: The spring holds. You seat the Movement and turn the collar. A tick. Another. The power reserve's needle slowly lifts off zero and keeps going.
James laughs. Once, short, surprised. Then he glances at the door, in case anyone heard.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: He clears his throat and fits the Dial back onto the umbrella handle, taking longer than it needs. "Adequate." A pause. "Better than adequate. Don't make me say it again."
The collar ticks between you. James hasn't let go of the umbrella.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.result_text: You say nothing. James appears grateful, as far as he is able.

choices.label: Point out that he laughed
choices.result_text: "I did not." He doesn't look up from the collar. "It was a cough."

choices.label: Ask how it feels
choices.result_text: He turns the collar one click and listens. "Familiar," he says, and leaves it there.

cards.text: He walks you to the door, which he has never done. "There's something else. I'll text you. And do turn up on time." The door closes down. Behind it, you hear the collar click twice.
